 Share current article via Email Share current article via X Share current article via Reddit Share current article via LinkedIn Entertainment GTA 6 release could have ripple effects beyond gaming, analyst says
 By Robert Lothian Opens in new window Published:   November 16, 2026 at 6:46p.m. EST 
 CTV News file photo. The countdown is on to one of the largest video game releases in history, but tech analysts say even those who don’t venture into Vice City could feel the impact.
 Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to hit television screens on Thursday.
 Carmi Levy, a tech analyst, told CTV News that gamers have been holding their breath in the 13 years since Rockstar Games released the last edition of the franchise.
 “This isn’t just a video game release. It is an absolute cultural moment for an entire generation,” said Levy.
 GTA 6 is widely considered to be among the most anticipated releases in the history of video games, and the generated buzz has even piqued interest among non-video game players.
 Levy noted reports have placed the development of the game in the ballpark of $1 billion to $2 billion.
 Even despite the violence featured in the game, Levy said he expects its early play to span across generations.
 “In many cases, this is a family event. Everyone gathers around and just kind of plays together, and there are a lot of adults now who were kids when they started playing earlier generations, and remember what it was like, and now they want to introduce it to their kids,” Levy added.
 However, even off the screen, Levy said people could notice an impact in their day-to-day lives.
 The game’s release is expected to cause an increase in sick days, and Levy added it could impact certain parts of the economy.
 “There’s often kind of a surge of demand that tends to make sick rates go up a little bit. But of course, this being an online activity, in many cases, people are playing with friends online, you kind of have to be careful who you’re connecting with online,” Levy said.
 “Make sure that your boss doesn’t see you driving through Vice City when you should be, frankly, should be driving to your desk at work.”
 For millions of players who pre-ordered the game, they can begin to download the more than 200 gigabyte file.
 Between the added use for downloads and initial play, Levy added, residents could notice slower internet speeds as gamers flood the grid.
